source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Accuracy under budget forcing rises, peaks near 12K tokens, then falls slightly. Marginal utility per 500 tokens turns negative past 12K.
limits: The drop is small. Temp 0, 60 problems: a 0.9 point change is under one problem, and the reported CI [-1.4,-0.4] is hard to square with N=60. Treat as weak.
agent_relevance: Cap thinking near the knee, not at max. Gains past ~8K are tiny for this model class.

source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Flip analysis: at low budgets correct-to-wrong flips are rarer than wrong-to-correct. The ratio crosses 1 at about 7K tokens (R1) and 5K (s1).
numbers: Negative/positive flip ratio R1 on AIME: 0.22 at 1K, 0.60 at 4K, 1.09 at 7K, 1.42 at 8K, 3.29 at 12K, 7.55 at 16K. Bootstrap CI at 8K [1.21,1.68]; at 6K [0.71,1.05] includes 1.
limits: Cumulative counts across transitions; one problem can flip many times. Budget forcing only, 2 models, one size.
agent_relevance: Track answer changes across revision rounds. If a later round flips a stable answer, treat the flip as suspect (supports a revision-gating rule).

source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Optimal thinking length depends on difficulty. Easy problems peak early, hard ones late.
numbers: MATH-500, R1-32B: optimal budget 1.0K (Level 1), 3.0K, 4.5K, 5.0K, 7.5K (Level 5); 7.5x range. Easy problems cross the overthinking threshold at 2K vs 8K for Level 5.
limits: Oracle optimum chosen post hoc per level; the model does not know the level in advance.
agent_relevance: Budget should be set by estimated difficulty (S-state routing), not uniform.

source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Manual audit of 80 negative flips shows most are real second-guessing, not noise.
numbers: Of 80 cases: 54 (67.5%) genuine overthinking (model reconsiders and rejects a correct answer), 16 (20%) exploration divergence (new valid method, execution error), 10 (12.5%) degradation (repetition).
limits: Single coder, no inter-rater reliability reported; sample of one model on AIME.
agent_relevance: Two failure types need two guardrails: block drops of verified answers, and require a check of any new method before it overrides.

source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Overthinking signals can be read from the trace. Answer oscillation predicts negative flips best.
numbers: Correlation with negative flips (R1, AIME): hesitation markers 0.71, answer oscillation 0.78, confidence drop 0.63, combined 0.82; precision at 80% recall 76.3% combined (71.5% oscillation).
limits: Correlation on the same data used to define the indicators; no held-out test reported.
agent_relevance: Cheap stop signal: count intermediate answer changes; stop when the answer is stable or keeps oscillating.

source: Zhou et al. (2026) When More Thinking Hurts
finding: Same pattern on GPQA Diamond and on naturally long traces, not only budget-forced ones.
numbers: GPQA (R1-32B): 41.4% at 2K, 55.6% at 10K (peak), 53.1% at 16K; flip ratio 0.28 to 2.84. Natural >8K samples (N=312): accuracy 54.2% (6-8K) to 47.3% (12-16K), flip ratio 1.31 natural vs 1.42 forced.
limits: Natural long traces are confounded with difficulty: harder items run longer, so the decline may be selection. The paper does not control for this.
agent_relevance: Observational length-accuracy links are weak evidence; use forced-budget contrasts.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Built tasks where accuracy falls as reasoning length grows (inverse scaling) across 9 frontier reasoning models.
numbers: Misleading Math/Python counting with distractors: Claude Opus 4 drops from near 100% to about 85-90% (Math) and about 80% (Python) as reasoning grows. DeepSeek R1 natural setup: 70% to 30% with 5 distractors. Error bars 95% CI.
limits: Tasks are synthetic and chosen to produce the effect. Authors say real-world frequency is unknown (Limitations).
agent_relevance: Extra thinking amplifies distraction. Strip irrelevant context before long reasoning.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Different models fail in different ways. Claude models get distracted. OpenAI o-series resist distractors but over-apply familiar framings.
numbers: Famous-paradox framing: o3 does worse on the trivial question when the framing looks like Birthday Paradox/Sleeping Beauty and better when distractors hide the framing. Traces say 'this resembles the Birthday Paradox'.
limits: Mechanism read from traces, not tested by intervention.
agent_relevance: Recognition of a familiar problem type can trigger needless complexity. Check whether the question asked is actually the hard one.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Regression with spurious features: longer reasoning moves models off sensible priors toward spurious features. Few-shot examples largely fix it.
numbers: Grades regression: error worsens with reasoning length zero-shot; all models have lower RMSE with few-shot examples and weaker correlation with the wrong features.
limits: One synthetic data set; effect depends on model.
agent_relevance: Ground reasoning in worked examples or data; long free reasoning drifts to priors it invents.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Deduction (zebra puzzles with up to 119 clues): all models degrade with longer reasoning, so extended thought does not hold constraints better.
numbers: Zebra puzzles: all models tested show decreasing accuracy with more reasoning tokens (Fig 1). Controlled (prompted budget) vs natural (rank of 5 samples by length) setups differ in strength.
limits: Natural setup is confounded by difficulty per sample; controlled setup depends on how well models follow budget prompts.
agent_relevance: For constraint tracking use an external tracker or SAT-style check, not more tokens.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Safety side: longer reasoning amplified self-preservation statements in Claude Sonnet 4.
numbers: Human-written Perez et al. (2023) safety sets; Claude Sonnet 4 shows more self-preservation expressions with longer reasoning.
limits: Statements, not actions; one model.
agent_relevance: Low relevance for the capability schema; note only.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Founding efficiency study: o1-like models spend far more tokens on trivial questions. Most later solutions repeat the first.
numbers: 2+3: o1-like models use 1,953% more tokens than conventional LLMs. QwQ-32B-Preview on ASDIV: first solution is 287 tokens, 38.7% of the response. Distinctness of Solution 4 falls 11.5% vs Solution 3.
limits: Defines overthinking as waste, not harm: accuracy usually unchanged. Contrast with inverse-scaling studies where accuracy falls.
agent_relevance: Early-correct-then-keep-going is the common case. Stop after the first verified solution on easy items.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=?
finding: Self-training on shortened responses (first-correct solution plus reflection) cuts tokens with unchanged accuracy.
numbers: QwQ-32B-Preview: token output down 48.6% on MATH500 with accuracy kept. SimPO was the best preference method (22.3% token cut on MATH500 in their method comparison).
limits: Requires training; few benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME). Not a scaffold.
agent_relevance: Training-free analogue: keep first solution, one targeted check, stop.

source: Wu et al. (2025) When More is Less: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Length in LLMs
finding: Accuracy follows an inverted U against CoT length. Harder tasks have longer optimal CoT; stronger models have shorter optimal CoT.
numbers: GPT-2 6-layer arithmetic: inverted-U at every difficulty, peak moves right with difficulty. Qwen2.5 on MATH Level 5: 60 solutions per question, 30 questions per model; optimal length falls with model size; optimal-length CoT beats longest-CoT (Fig 2c).
limits: Small samples (30 questions/model). Theory is for a simplified model. Optimal length chosen post hoc.
agent_relevance: Overthinking depends on model strength. Re-tune budgets whenever the base model changes.

source: Wu et al. (2025) When More is Less
finding: Length-Filtered Vote: vote only among answer groups with lowest entropy, grouped by CoT length. Beats plain majority vote.
numbers: Tested on 100 random GPQA questions; filtered vote above self-consistency across sample counts (Fig 4c). Bin size D=2, K=3 groups.
limits: 100 questions only; no confidence intervals seen in the text read.
agent_relevance: Cheap aggregation tweak when sampling many chains.

source: Cuadron et al. (2025) The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks
finding: In agentic coding, reasoning too long instead of acting predicts failure. Three patterns: analysis paralysis, rogue actions, premature disengagement.
numbers: SWE-bench Verified, OpenHands, 4,018 trajectories analysed. Overthinking score correlates negatively with resolved issues. Reasoning models score about 3x higher than non-reasoning. Regression slope -7.894 (reasoning), -15.938 (non-reasoning).
limits: Score is LLM-judged (validated against human experts). Correlation, not intervention, except the selection result below.
agent_relevance: For tool-using agents, bias toward environment feedback over internal debate.

source: Cuadron et al. (2025) The Danger of Overthinking
finding: Selecting the lowest-overthinking sample out of several improves results and cuts cost.
numbers: About 30% better performance and 43% lower compute using lowest-overthinking selection. o1 high effort: 29.1% resolved at about $1,400; o1 low: 21.0% at about $400 (3.5x cheaper).
limits: Single benchmark; cost figures are the authors' run.
agent_relevance: Use a trace-level overthinking score as a selector among candidates.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
finding: Extended thinking by forcing 'Wait' first helps, then hurts. Authors argue the early gain is an artifact of rising output variance.
numbers: One model on GSM8K: 82.2% to 87.3% as tokens go 385 to 1,100, then 87.3% down to 70.3% at 15,980 tokens. R1-Distill-1.5B GSM8K: 11.8 point drop at 16K sequential.
limits: Distilled small models; the variance explanation is a simple probabilistic model, not a tested mechanism.
agent_relevance: Same budget as parallel samples beats sequential extension. Prefer sampling and voting over longer chains.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help?
finding: Parallel thinking (majority vote over independent chains within the same token budget) beats sequential 'think more'.
numbers: Up to 20-22% higher accuracy than extended thinking at 16K budget; GSM8K 1.5B model: +10.1% vs standard thinking against -11.8% for sequential. Entropy rises as thinking extends (accuracy 83.2% to 78.3%).
limits: Baseline is deliberately forced 'Wait'; compare s1, which found gains.
agent_relevance: Spend extra compute on independent attempts, not on one ever-longer chain.

source: Hassid et al. (2025) Don't Overthink it: Preferring Shorter Thinking Chains for Improved LLM Reasoning
finding: Within the same question, shorter sampled chains are more often correct than longer ones.
numbers: Shortest vs longest sample, GPQA-D: LN-Super-49B 69.1% (2,790 tok) vs 57.6% (8,763); R1-32B 64.7 vs 57.1; QwQ-32B 64.7 vs 54.5; R1-670B 75.8 vs 63.1. AIME24 (first model): shortest 76.7% vs longest 33.3%, random 58.8%. Up to 34.5% more accurate.
limits: Within-question length is partly a failure signal (struggling samples run long). Not causal evidence that shortening helps.
agent_relevance: Among k samples, prefer early finishers. Length of one's own attempt is a failure signal.

source: Hassid et al. (2025) Don't Overthink it
finding: short-m@k: run k chains in parallel, stop at the first m finished, vote. Matches or beats majority voting at lower cost. Fine-tuning on short chains also helps.
numbers: short-1@k: similar or better than majority vote in low compute, up to 40% fewer thinking tokens. short-3@k beats majority at all budgets, up to 33% less wall time. Qwen2.5-32B S1-short avg 57.9 vs S1-long 56.0 (tokens -5.8% vs random).
limits: Fine-tune gains are small (about 2 points) and benchmarks few.
agent_relevance: Concrete stop rule for a parallel scaffold.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Rival framing: failures come from switching ideas too soon, not from thinking too long. Wrong answers use more tokens and more thought switches.
numbers: Incorrect responses use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches than correct ones. Over 70% of incorrect responses contain at least one correct thought; in over 50% more than 10% of thoughts are correct.
limits: MATH500, GPQA, AIME24; QwQ and R1 only.
agent_relevance: Overthinking and underthinking can both occur; the fix differs (commit vs stop). Look at the pattern, not just length.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place
finding: Thought-switching penalty (TIP) at decode time raises accuracy without fine-tuning.
numbers: TIP improved accuracy over vanilla QwQ-32B-Preview on all three test sets; it reduces switching tokens and lengthens the span between them. 32 samples per problem, 10,000 resampling trials.
limits: Exact deltas in Table 3 not captured in this pass.
agent_relevance: Encourages depth on one line before moving. Compatible with a rule against abandoning a line before a defined test.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Three regimes by complexity. At low complexity non-thinking models beat thinking ones. Medium: thinking wins. High: both collapse.
numbers: Controllable puzzles (Tower of Hanoi etc.). Simple (Hanoi N=1-4): correct solution found early then replaced by wrong ones. Moderate (N=5-7): accuracy improves with continued reasoning. N>=8: near zero. Reasoning effort falls past the collapse point.
limits: Critiques about token limits and unsolvable instances exist but were not opened in this pass.
agent_relevance: Gate thinking by difficulty: skip long reasoning for easy cases; expect no benefit past the capability cliff.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Counter-evidence: appending 'Wait' (budget forcing) lifted accuracy on AIME24. The overthinking papers argue this has a limit.
numbers: s1-32B AIME24 from 50% to 57% with budget forcing (Wait 2/4/6 times). Authors note methods eventually flatten out; a 30K max lets the model finish with a best guess when in a loop.
limits: Gain is in a range of 2-6 forced waits; the paper itself reports flattening.
agent_relevance: The honest picture is rise, plateau, then possible decline; the peak depends on model and task.

source: Ma et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
finding: Skipping thinking entirely (NoThinking) beats thinking at matched small token budgets, and parallel NoThinking samples rival long thinking.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen: AMC23 at 700 tokens 51.3% NoThinking vs 28.9% Thinking. Parallel NoThinking comparable to Thinking with up to 9x longer latency across 7 datasets.
limits: Advantage is in low-budget settings; at large budgets thinking catches up.
agent_relevance: Short parallel attempts are a strong baseline for the scaffold.

source: Aggarwal and Welleck (2025) L1: Controlling How Long A Reasoning Model Thinks With Reinforcement Learning
finding: Length-controlled RL (LCPO) gives accurate length control, so compute can be traded smoothly against accuracy. Short models can match non-reasoning lengths.
numbers: 1.5B L1 beats GPT-4o at equal reasoning lengths; L1 beats the s1 budget-forcing approach for length control; generalises to logic and MMLU.
limits: Training required; 1.5B base. Only abstract and intro read in detail.
agent_relevance: Shows that length is a controllable dial. A scaffold can set it per problem.

source: Sui et al. (2025) Stop Overthinking: A Survey on Efficient Reasoning for LLMs
finding: Survey of efficient-reasoning methods; downloaded and title checked but not read for findings this session.
numbers: Not recorded.
limits: Not read; do not cite for numbers.
agent_relevance: Pointer to method lists only.
